description.narrative: The project is implemented in Philippines. The main outcome area it contributes to is equality and worker's rights and Just transition. The main rights holders are the workers in these sectors. Through education and supporting organising capacity the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcomes areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is administred by LEARN but the project activities are carried out by Fishworkers Solidarity, POWER- the national union for employees in the energy sector, and PEUP -the union for postal employees. Swedish union Seko has many years of experience of organising and union work within the same sectors in Sweden and participates in the project through strategic planning and overall implementation, as well as by providing trainings or workshops.The fishing communities and their livelihoods are vulnerable to coastal hazards and the impact of unsustainable coastal development practices such as to overfishing and pollution. Some fishing communities also are facing threats of displacements to give way to building resorts for tourism and fish industry development.The project activities with POWER focuses on providing affordable green, sustainable and non-for-profit electricity to communities, and decent working conditions. The situation in the energy industry needs to change to the better, as it is negatively affecting the consumers and workers in the industry. Fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas supply about 80 percent of the countrys energy needs. The Philippines has abundant indigenous energy sources, particularly geothermal and biomass but these are not fully utilised for lack of financial investments. The energy mix is dominated primarily by imported coal. Fear of insufficient electricity supply looms with the likelihood of limited coal imports, depletion of its natural gas supply, slow growth of renewable energy utilisation, and aging power facilities.Other Donors to the OrganisationThere are no other donors to this projectProject ObjectiveThe project aims to consolidate and expand social movement unionism in all three sectors to enable workers to access their trade union and workers' rights and improve their well-being and a shift toward a just transition. Building strong, democratic, resilient and self-sufficient unions capable of defending and advancing the rights and welfare of the workers would be the key requirement to address the low union density in the 3 sectors commercial and subsistence fishing, postal service, and the electric power industry.Actor groupsThe main actors within actor group decision-makers" are various government agencies such as Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), the Civil Service Commission (CSC), the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA), the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), the Department of Energy (DOE) and the National Electrification Administration (NEA), as well as the two chambers of the Congress. The main actors working in cooperation for this project are SENTROS affiliated Trade Unions (30 affiliates), the Labor Education and Research Network (LEARN), Global Union Federations like Public Services International (PSI) and the International Union of Food and Allied Workers (IUF) The main actors within actor group rightsholders are their individual trade union members."
